Privacy

What this server stores, what it can read, and what it would have to hand over if somebody with a court order asked.

Written to be checkable. Every claim below matches something in the code or the database schema. Where a protection has a limit, the limit is stated rather than left out. A privacy policy that overstates its protections isn't a stronger policy — it's one that falls apart the first time anybody tests it.
{# ====================================================== the short version #}

The short version

{{ icons.shield() }} No third parties
  • Nothing here is sold, shared, or used to train anything.
  • There is no advertising, no tracking pixel, and no third-party script. The page you're reading loads nothing from outside this server.
  • The only counting that happens anywhere is a per-link total on creator support links, and an operator-only dashboard that adds up rows already listed below. Neither builds a profile of you.
  • Direct messages are encrypted in your browser. This server stores ciphertext it holds no key for.
  • Plenty of other things are stored — comments, likes, watch history, room posts. They're listed below.
{# ============================================================ encryption #}

Direct messages

{{ icons.lock() }} End-to-end

Your browser generates an ECDH P-256 key pair. The public half is uploaded so others can encrypt to you. The private half is encrypted with AES-GCM under a key derived from a passphrase by PBKDF2 (600,000 iterations) and only then uploaded. This server stores the encrypted result, the nonce, and the derivation parameters.

The passphrase never leaves your browser. Not at sign-up, not at sign-in, not in any request. It is deliberately separate from your account password, because this server necessarily sees your account password when you sign in — a vault locked with a password the server sees would be a vault the server could open.

Each message is encrypted with a key derived from your private key and the recipient's public key. Only the two of you can compute it. What is written to the database is a base64 blob and a nonce.

What this does not protect.
  • Metadata. That you messaged a particular person, and when, is stored in the clear. Delivering a message means knowing where to send it. No design avoids this.
  • Forward secrecy. There is one long-lived key pair per account and no ratchet. If your passphrase is compromised, your whole message history is readable.
  • Key substitution. This server hands out public keys. A malicious operator could hand out one they hold the private half of. Compare fingerprints with the other person somewhere other than here — that check is why they're displayed.
  • Your own devices. Encryption stops at the screen. Anyone with access to your unlocked browser can read your messages.

If you lose the passphrase, your messages are gone. No administrator can recover them. That is the same property as "the operator can't read them", seen from the other side.

{# ================================================================ stored #}

What is stored, in full

{{ icons.info() }} Readable by the operator

Everything below lives in one SQLite file on this machine and is readable by whoever runs this server. This is the honest list, not the flattering one.

StoredWhy
Username and password hash Sign-in. The password itself is not stored — only a PBKDF2-SHA256 hash of it.
Display name and bio Whatever you chose to put there.
Sessions A hash of your session token, plus expiry, browser user agent, and IP address. See the note below on turning the last two off.
Comments and video responses Plain text, publicly visible on this server.
Room posts Plain text, readable by every account here.
Likes, dislikes, subscriptions, playlists So the features work at all.
Watch history and resume positions Continue watching, and recommendations. Can be paused in settings.
Search history Search suggestions. Can be paused and cleared.
Notifications Titles and short previews. A message notification never contains message text — this server has never seen it.
Message metadata Who, with whom, when, read or unread. Not content.
Uploaded files Video responses and Studio uploads sit on this disk.
Creator link opens A single running total per support, merch, or affiliate link, so a creator can tell whether it works. No account, no timestamp, and no row per click is stored — the table has no column that could say who opened a link, so that question can't be answered from it by anyone, including whoever runs this server.
{# =============================================================== leaving #}

What leaves this machine

{{ icons.search() }}
Search queries
Sent to YouTube and Tubi when you search, the same as typing into their own search boxes.
{{ icons.film() }}
Stream requests
yt-dlp fetches the video from its source so it can play here. That request carries this server's IP address, not yours.
{{ icons.upload() }}
Videos you publish from Studio
Only when you explicitly upload one, and only to the Google account you connected yourself.

Nothing social leaves. Commenting here does not comment on YouTube. Liking here does not like there. Messages and room posts never leave this machine at all.

{# ================================================================== legal #}

Legal requests

Read this part carefully

You may have seen services claim they cannot be compelled to produce anything. That claim is almost always wrong, and it is worth being precise about instead.

A valid legal order reaches whatever the operator actually holds. Not what a policy page says they hold. So the only real protection is the data that was never collected, or that exists in a form nobody can read.

If compelled, could be producedStatus
Message content Ciphertext only
Producible, but unreadable. No key exists on this server to decrypt it.
Who messaged whom, and when Producible
Comments and room posts Producible in full
Watch and search history Producible in full
Which links you opened Not stored
Only a total per link, with nobody attached to it.
Username, IP addresses, session records Producible
Your password Not stored
Only a slow hash. Not reversible.
Your message passphrase Never received

This is a description of how the software stores data, not legal advice, and it isn't a commitment about how any particular operator will respond to any particular request. If you are running this server for other people, what you can be made to hand over depends on your jurisdiction — talk to a lawyer rather than relying on a page inside your own app.

{# ================================================================ control #}

Turning things off

  • Pause history — Settings. Stops watch and search history being written at all.
  • Clear history — Settings, and the History page. Deletes what's already there.
  • Delete a conversation — removes it for both people, permanently.
  • Lock your key — removes it from this browser without deleting anything on the server.
  • Block someone — stops their messages and hides their room posts from you.
  • Server operators — STORE_SESSION_IP=0 in .env stops IP addresses and user agents being recorded with sessions.

The Hub v{{ app_version }} · This page describes this build. If you change how data is handled, change this page too.
